messages:
jessica_pm: quick heads-up — want to triage the acceptance criteria for tool/function-calling output v1. Customers A+B hit integration failures where the model returns slightly malformed JSON and our current fallback is too aggressive. can we align on requirements + launch gates?
ryan_eng: adding context — failures are usually missing required fields or arrays returned as strings. current validator rejects and we fall back to text-only. causes major regressions for customers expecting structured data.
sam_ml: thanks. from modeling side we can tighten sampling+prompting to reduce malformation, but we need clear contract: what errors trigger retry vs fallback vs pass-through?
jessica_pm: propose v1 acceptance: 1) explicit schema validation (jsonschema) with well-defined error codes; 2) graceful degraded payload that includes original text + best-effort parsed fields; 3) observability: breakdown of validation failures by error code; 4) rollout canary + automatic rollback on >X% regression. thoughts?
tara_ux: for UX, need a clear field in response: `parsing_quality: "ok/warn/error"` and `parsing_errors: []` so integrators can show a banner instead of blank UI. keep structures small.
omar_qa: QA checklist: unit tests for all edgecases, integration tests with synthetic malformed outputs, e2e with sample customer prompts, and a smoke test that validates our fallback preserves privacy (no leaking prompt tokens into logs).
alyssa_legal: confirm: any fallback that returns the original model text must be filtered for PII and have TTL for retention. add KMS flag for encrypted logs if enterprise.
ryan_eng: implementation note: runtime can do a 2-pass approach: attempt parse -> if fails, run a constrained parser/repair step (max 200ms) -> if still fails, emit degraded payload. repair step could be regex-based heuristics. code sketch: ```js const repair = (s) => s.replace(/\"\"/g, '"'); // naive example```
sam_ml: we should avoid heavy heuristics that mask model failure. prefer deterministic, well-documented repairs and make repair logs auditable. also tie into quality monitor to catch regressions.
jessica_pm: launch gates proposal: - low-risk canary (1% of traffic) for 48h, - target metrics: validation_fail_rate <= 0.5% and end-user error surface <= 0.1% (tracked via QA harness). if regressions, auto-roll back.
omar_qa: I'll own the QA harness and create synthetic prompt corpora (happy/malformed/adversarial). need naming conventions for synthetic tests.
tara_ux: for API changes, add `parsing_quality` enum + `parsing_errors` list of short codes. docs snippet: ```json { "parsing_quality": "warn", "parsing_errors": ["MISSING_FIELD_ts", "ARRAY_AS_STRING"] } ```
alyssa_legal: add a short glossary of error codes for compliance reviewers. avoid codes that imply user-identifiable data was exposed.
ryan_eng: operationally: add metrics: validation_fail_count, repair_attempt_count, degraded_response_count, avg_repair_latency. emit events to tracing with trace_id.
deply_bot: deploy_bot: scheduled canary rollout window 2026-05-04T09:00Z -> 2026-05-06T09:00Z. automated rollback threshold: degraded_response_count_rate > 0.001 over 5m
jessica_pm: action items: @omar_qa build harness + deliver by EOD Wed; @ryan_eng prototype repair step + PR with config flags; @sam_ml provide prompt set + model-side tweaks; @tara_ux draft API docs and error glossary; @alyssa_legal review retention & PII wording. we’ll reconvene Thu 10am to sign off.
ryan_eng: ack — will include a feature flag so we can toggle repair heuristics independently.
sam_ml: will also add evals that score parsing_quality over historical prompts to baseline before canary.
omar_qa: creating ticket and sample corpus now, will link when ready.
jessica_pm: thanks all. small ask — keep messages short in this thread. we want a concise record for the PRD. :thumbsup:
